title: Spiritualism wave: seances as common as church

plain: Tim Alberino, a filmmaker and researcher, describes a craze in the late 1800s and early 1900s for spiritualism, the practice of trying to contact the dead. He says magazine and newspaper articles from that time, which he gathered for a project called Birthright, claimed that at its height an American was as likely to go to a seance, a gathering to speak with spirits, on Sunday morning as to go to church. He tells it to show how common contact with the unseen once seemed to ordinary people.
